package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability due to improper sanitization of user-supplied Markdown input. Specifically, it fails to correctly filter or block links with obfuscated 'javascript:' protocols (e.g., using HTML entities), allowing attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser context when user input is rendered as HTML. This enables attackers to perform XSS attacks, potentially leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or other malicious actions in affected applications.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user-supplied Markdown is rendered to HTML)
execution_context.file_location: application code that uses the marked library to render user input (e.g., note rendering logic in Goof or similar applications)
required_permissions: DOM access (browser context for script execution)
network (if XSS payload exfiltrates data via HTTP requests)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user-supplied Markdown is rendered to HTML, the code processes a crafted Markdown link with an obfuscated 'javascript:' protocol using an HTML entity for the colon. The marked package fails to sanitize this input, resulting in an HTML anchor tag with an href attribute that the browser interprets as executable JavaScript. When a user clicks the link, the browser executes the attacker's JavaScript payload, leading to XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The input is crafted to bypass sanitization by encoding the colon in 'javascript:' as '&#58', which is decoded by the browser but not recognized as dangerous by the sanitizer. This allows execution of arbitrary JavaScript when the link is clicked.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Markdown rendering libraries are expected to sanitize or block dangerous protocols like 'javascript:' in link hrefs, even when obfuscated with HTML entities, especially when the sanitize option is enabled. Here, the sanitizer fails to decode and block the obfuscated protocol, violating security expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Markdown links should only use safe protocols such as 'http', 'https', or 'mailto', and should never allow JavaScript execution via links. Encoding characters in the protocol part of a link is not a common or legitimate use case.
key_indicators: Markdown links with hrefs containing 'javascript:' or entity-encoded variants (e.g., 'javascript:')
HTML anchor tags in rendered output with href attributes starting with 'javascript:' or containing HTML entity-encoded characters
User input containing suspicious HTML entities in the protocol portion of Markdown links
Sanitizer fails to remove or neutralize links with obfuscated JavaScript protocols

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits user input containing a crafted Markdown link with an obfuscated JavaScript protocol, such as [Gotcha](javascript&#58this;alert(1)), to the vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious Markdown input is stored or processed by the application.

attack_chain.action: The application uses the marked library to render the user-supplied Markdown to HTML, with the sanitize option enabled. The sanitizer fails to detect and block the obfuscated JavaScript protocol in the link.
attack_chain.leads_to: The rendered HTML output contains an <a> tag with an href attribute that starts with 'javascript:' (decoded from the HTML entity), making it executable in the browser.

attack_chain.action: A user views the rendered content and clicks the malicious link, causing the browser to execute the attacker's JavaScript payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cross-site scripting (XSS) is triggered, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser context.

behavioral_signatures: Markdown links with href attributes containing 'javascript:' or any HTML entity-encoded variant (e.g., 'javascript:')
Rendered HTML containing <a> tags with href attributes that start with 'javascript:' or contain HTML entities in the protocol
User input with suspicious HTML entities in the protocol portion of Markdown links (e.g., ':' in place of ':')
Sanitizer output that fails to remove or neutralize links with obfuscated JavaScript protocols
file_indicators: User-supplied Markdown content containing patterns like [text](javascript:...) or [text](javascript:...)
HTML output files or DOM containing <a href="javascript:..."> or <a href="javascript:...">
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests initiated by user interaction with rendered links in user-generated content
Browser requests to attacker-controlled domains following clicks on links in rendered Markdown content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan rendered HTML for anchor tags with href attributes that begin with 'javascript:' or any HTML entity-encoded variant (such as 'javascript:'). Monitor user input for Markdown links containing suspicious protocols or encoded characters in the protocol portion. Ensure that the Markdown renderer's sanitizer decodes and blocks all forms of 'javascript:' links, including those obfuscated with HTML entities. Automated detection systems should flag any occurrence of anchor tags with hrefs that resolve to JavaScript execution, regardless of encoding.
